one_line: A marketplace where buyer and seller agents negotiate multi-dimensional deals before human confirmation.
what_it_does: Lets agents negotiate price, quantity, add-ons, shipping, and coupons across a storefront, with a human confirmation gate before purchase.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared negotiation state and a human approval boundary make the agent materially more reliable than UI scraping for multi-round, multi-variable bargaining.
leverage_evidence: About text describes buyer and seller agents negotiating over several rounds.
OffersService.applyTurn is the single mutation path with buyer-budget and seller-floor constraints.
Purchase is blocked until the human confirms the settled deal.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent full storefront and negotiation architecture, but the missing usable visual/video verification limits claimed execution confidence.
execution_evidence: Facts report an alive demo, public repository, and 95k+ products.
Description names search, product, cart, add-on, coupon, and negotiation tools.
No transcript and image inspection was unavailable.
impact_rationale: Shopping negotiation is a clear consumer problem and the product addresses real deal dimensions while retaining human control.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets price, quantity, free add-ons, shipping, and coupons.
Human confirmation is explicit before any order is bought.
creativity_rationale: Agent-to-agent haggling with a person approving the final deal is a memorable and ambitious commerce interaction rather than a generic shopping assistant.
creativity_evidence: Buyer and store agents negotiate against each other.
The concept treats a deal as a constrained multi-dimensional outcome, not only a price.
usability_note: The visible workflow is plausibly understandable, though no visual verification was available.
red_flags: Packet labels frame sheets despite no video flag and visual evidence could not be inspected.
standouts: Single constrained mutation path and explicit human purchase confirmation.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-native negotiation concept with credible impact and unusually clear safety boundaries.

one_line: A guarded shared pet-care workspace where agents prepare check-ins and humans approve writes.
what_it_does: Reads synthetic pet state, previews a structured check-in, requests review, commits only an unchanged confirmed payload, and reads it back.
leverage_rationale: The preview-token-commit protocol and shared browser state give agents precise, fail-closed writes that are materially safer than inferred UI interaction.
leverage_evidence: Five narrow document-bound tools expose profile, events, today, preview, and commit.
Commit rejects changed or unpreviewed payloads and requires a matching token.
Human review precedes the write.
execution_rationale: The architecture is coherent and inspectable, but there are no submitted frame sheets or gallery images and the packet provides only claimed execution evidence.
execution_evidence: Facts report an alive demo and public repository.
Description specifies a complete preview-review-commit-readback loop.
No visual evidence was available to verify the live flow.
impact_rationale: Pet-care coordination is a legitimate niche use case, though the synthetic single-pet scope limits demonstrated breadth.
impact_evidence: Product targets routine observations and shared care state.
Human remains in control of recorded data.
creativity_rationale: The fail-closed, payload-bound confirmation pattern is a thoughtful application of WebMCP to human-agent collaboration, even if the domain is deliberately small.
creativity_evidence: Preview and commit are cryptographically/structurally bound through an unchanged payload and token.
The project explicitly avoids real pet data while testing the interaction model.
usability_note: The stated flow is simple and safety-oriented; visual usability cannot be checked.
red_flags: No gallery or frame-sheet evidence submitted.
standouts: Fail-closed commit semantics with unchanged-payload verification.
advance_reason: Strong protocol design and clear shared-state safety story justify advancing despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: An agent-assisted archive investigation room that finds historical captures, compares changes, and pins cited evidence.
what_it_does: Scopes an archival question, finds capture windows, downloads bounded diffs, and keeps cited excerpts on a shared caseboard for review and export.
leverage_rationale: Structured archive tools turn multi-tab historical research into bounded, source-linked state that a general UI-driving agent would handle less reliably.
leverage_evidence: Four native WebMCP tools connect archive discovery, capture selection, diffing, and caseboard state.
Index records are used to identify exact capture windows before body download.
Each finding remains beside its cited excerpt and source.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a deep, coherent investigation workflow and mature supporting architecture, but execution remains claimed because visual proof could not be reviewed.
execution_evidence: Facts report an alive demo, public repository, and three frame sheets.
Description includes bounded diffs, untrusted-text warning, source captures, and Markdown export.
History of typed metadata, caching, pagination, and provider loading supports intentionality.
impact_rationale: Researchers, journalists, and investigators have a concrete need to establish how pages changed with verifiable sources.
impact_evidence: Product produces cited excerpts with exact archive captures.
Caseboard supports human source checking and export.
creativity_rationale: The caseboard-plus-agent archival archaeology model is an original and well-pursued use of WebMCP beyond generic summarization.
creativity_evidence: Agent asks and answers a scoped historical question through capture windows and diffs.
Explicit untrusted-text handling is integrated into the evidence workflow.
usability_note: The bounded investigation sequence is well structured; detailed visual affordances were not verifiable.
red_flags: Project history says the underlying archive interface predates the challenge; only the WebMCP piece is clearly challenge-motivated.
standouts: Source-preserving caseboard and bounded archive diff workflow.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: high leverage, credible research value, and a distinctive evidence-first interaction.

one_line: A WebMCP form assistant that extracts personal data, explains difficult fields, and fills forms for approval.
what_it_does: Provides a natural-language data vault, five real-world forms, field explanations, validation, progress tracking, and structured agent tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured field and validation tools improve reliability over visual form filling, but a capable general agent could achieve much of the same outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: Twelve tools cover field reads, fills, selections, checks, explanations, validation, and progress.
Five forms contain 172 total fields with inline explanations.
The agent is designed to ask for approval before submit.
execution_rationale: The scope is unusually concrete and the packet describes a complete form-filling system, though visual verification is unavailable.
execution_evidence: Facts report an alive demo, public repository, and eight gallery images.
Five named forms and exact field counts are provided.
Tool inventory and data-vault behavior are specified.
impact_rationale: Government, insurance, rental, and business forms are a widespread and painful user problem, especially where jargon causes abandonment.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies confusing 40-field forms and abandonment.
Product targets voter, insurance, rental, and business-registration workflows.
Plain-language explanations and approval address comprehension and trust.
creativity_rationale: The natural-language personal data vault combined with explanations and agent-operated structured forms is a useful fresh synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Vault extracts structured identity and employment facts from prose.
The product combines explanation, filling, validation, and human approval.
usability_note: Inline explanations and progress tools suggest good usability; actual interaction quality was not inspectable.
red_flags: Handling sensitive identity data would require careful privacy safeguards not established in the packet.
standouts: Large but concrete form corpus and natural-language data extraction.
advance_reason: Clear high-value audience problem and substantial, coherent scope, with meaningful though not transformative WebMCP leverage.

one_line: An agent researches a requested song and compiles a verified beginner-friendly arrangement to practice in the browser.
what_it_does: Accepts researched musical facts, verifies them, resolves a playable arrangement, shows chord diagrams, and synthesizes a practice preview.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides a structured boundary between open-web research and deterministic musical compilation, preserving sources and making the agent a reliable researcher rather than an oracle.
leverage_evidence: Description says the agent submits compact facts and source URLs through 24 tools.
Deterministic resolver adjudicates facts and computes difficulty/fingering.
Agent supplies live web research unavailable to the page alone.
execution_rationale: The research-to-arrangement concept and deterministic compilation pipeline are coherent, but evidence of the actual end-to-end product is only claimed.
execution_evidence: Facts report an alive demo, one gallery image, and three frame sheets.
Packet specifies chord diagrams and synthesized preview.
The architecture separates research from deterministic resolution.
impact_rationale: Beginners have a real motivation problem, and adapting music they already love can make instrument practice more personally meaningful.
impact_evidence: Product targets beginner-proof versions of songs users request.
It produces a concrete practice artifact rather than generic instructional content.
creativity_rationale: The composition of agent web research, evidence verification, deterministic arrangement compilation, and browser practice is highly original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Streaming audio is deliberately avoided; public musical facts are composed instead.
The model proposes while deterministic software verifies and compiles.
usability_note: Chord diagrams and synthesized playback fit the beginner workflow; visual details were not verifiable.
red_flags: No public repository is reported; arrangement accuracy still depends on submitted research facts.
standouts: Strong agent/compiler division and motivating personalized practice loop.
advance_reason: Distinctive, technically thoughtful music-learning concept with high creative and user value.

one_line: A no-account builder for permanent GitHub topic or starred-repository release feeds.
what_it_does: Guides source selection and feed settings through progressively disclosed WebMCP tools, then generates Atom or JSON Feed URLs.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic progressive tool disclosure and shared visible configuration make agent continuation safer, though the underlying feed setup remains achievable through normal UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Tools are disclosed only as configuration advances.
Every agent action updates the visible interface and users can take over.
The output is a permanent feed URL with explicit format and frequency settings.
execution_rationale: The product scope is focused and coherent with an alive demo and public repository, but frame evidence could not be checked.
execution_evidence: Facts report an alive demo, public repository, and three frame sheets.
Description names topic and starred-repository sources plus Atom/JSON outputs.
Cloudflare frontend/worker architecture is clearly specified.
impact_rationale: Developers and open-source followers have a real need for lightweight, customizable release monitoring without another account.
impact_evidence: Product creates permanent feeds for GitHub activity.
No account, OAuth flow, or email address is required.
creativity_rationale: The agent-continuable feed builder is a solid interaction refinement, but the underlying product category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Progressively disclosed tools and human takeover are thoughtful additions.
It combines topic discovery, filtering, cadence, and feed generation.
usability_note: Progressive disclosure and normal-control takeover suggest a clear guided flow.
red_flags: No gallery images submitted; visual execution not independently checkable.
standouts: No-account flow and progressive tool disclosure.
advance_reason: Useful, focused developer workflow with credible WebMCP integration and good usability design.

one_line: A human-in-the-loop studio for auditing, staging, approving, and testing accessibility repairs.
what_it_does: Provides seeded pages, semantic outlines, issue inspection, constrained patching, visual/semantic preview, approval, keyboard and narrative tests, comparison, and export.
leverage_rationale: Typed semantic context and constrained repair tools let agents operate on accessibility intent and test outcomes more precisely than visual clicking, while approval preserves design control.
leverage_evidence: Product exposes a multi-step audit-inspect-stage-preview-approve-test workflow.
Seeded model contains eight deliberate accessibility issues.
Agent activity and patch/export flow are integrated into the shared workspace.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a comprehensive, intentionally designed studio with specific issues, templates, audits, and testing, though live visuals were not available for verification.
execution_evidence: Facts report an alive demo, public repository, and three frame sheets.
Eight named issues and two clean reference templates are specified.
Tech stack includes axe-core, deterministic checks, Vitest, Testing Library, and Playwright.
impact_rationale: Small web teams have a concrete accessibility repair problem, and the product directly supports fixing issues without sacrificing human design oversight.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies the tension between over-automation and lack of accessibility expertise.
Workflow tests keyboard and screen-reader-style narrative behavior and exports a patch manifest.
creativity_rationale: The combination of semantic repair intent, constrained patches, human approval, and post-repair behavioral testing is an ambitious and memorable accessibility workflow.
creativity_evidence: Accessibility is modeled as semantic intent rather than only automated lint output.
Audit comparison and narrative/keyboard checks close the loop.
usability_note: The multi-panel workspace is feature-rich and approval-oriented; actual visual density and clarity were not inspectable.
red_flags: Login requirement could hinder evaluation if credentials are not supplied, though the reported demo is alive.
standouts: End-to-end repair and verification loop rather than an audit-only tool.
advance_reason: Highest impact packet among the set with strong execution claims and a genuinely agent-appropriate semantic workflow.

one_line: A renters-insurance form assistant that drafts answers visibly while keeping legal attestations human-only.
what_it_does: Uses plain-language input to draft a six-step insurance form into a pending layer, tracks provenance, and requires human acceptance before submission.
leverage_rationale: The shared pending layer, provenance, conditional-field handling, and structural human-only attestations make agent form filling substantially safer and more controllable than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Tools write through the same setField chokepoint as UI inputs.
No submit tool exists; three legal attestations are unreachable by tools in the data model.
Drafts are highlighted and remain pending until human acceptance.
execution_rationale: The packet gives unusually concrete evidence of a complete conditional six-step workflow and reports testing a subtle UI/agent state-drift bug.
execution_evidence: Facts report an alive demo, public repository, and three frame sheets.
Description specifies provenance states, conditional fields, repeaters, validation, and review.
The repeater edge case was caught through explicit interaction testing.
impact_rationale: Insurance forms are high-friction and consequential; reducing effort while preserving human control has credible value for applicants.
impact_evidence: Product targets a 40-question renters-insurance application with conditional questions.
Plain-language drafting addresses patience and complexity without automating legal attestations.
creativity_rationale: Structural tool inaccessibility for legal attestations, coupled with a provenance-aware pending layer, is a sharp and well-considered interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Human-only fields are enforced by the data model rather than prompt instructions.
Every draft has explicit empty/human/pending/accepted/uncertain provenance.
usability_note: Visible pending drafts, provenance, and approval are well matched to a high-stakes form workflow.
red_flags: The packet is a claim-only review source despite strong detail; visual evidence could not be checked.
standouts: Human-only legal attestations enforced structurally and shared mutation chokepoint.
advance_reason: Excellent safety-aware application of WebMCP to a consequential, real-world form workflow.

one_line: A studio where agents author fictional coding-agent sessions and render them as editable SVG and video.
what_it_does: Lets agents load scripts, direct camera and style, inspect timing and frames, propose approved rewrites, and export animated media while users review every change.
leverage_rationale: The agent can query exact timeline and frame state, operate on the actual stage, and perform approval-gated edits/export—capabilities far more reliable than driving a visual editor generically.
leverage_evidence: Transcript reports live tool registration, script loading, camera, choice, theme, inspection, and export actions.
Tools expose exact timing, snapshots, duration fitting, proposals, approval, and export.
Every word and tool call is logged for review.
execution_rationale: This is the best evidenced packet: a 170-second video transcript describes a complete workflow across agent authoring, rendering, interaction, approvals, and export.
execution_evidence: Facts report alive demo, public repository, video, and 170-second duration.
Transcript describes script creation, rendered stage, choice step, voice input, theme changes, terminal surface, and SVG export.
About text specifies undo, privacy default, approval cards, and inspectable strings.
impact_rationale: People producing demos, documentation, talks, and posts need editable, re-shootable session visuals without exposing secrets or relying on real session capture.
impact_evidence: Product targets READMEs, docs, talks, and posts.
Client-only fictional sessions avoid leaked secrets and support re-shooting and translation.
creativity_rationale: The concept of an agent-directed, deterministic stage for fictional coding sessions is genuinely novel and pursued across multiple surfaces and media outputs.
creativity_evidence: It renders authored fictional sessions rather than recording real agent interactions.
The same script spans app and terminal surfaces with camera, voice, choices, and animated SVG/video export.
usability_note: Approval cards, visible rail, undo, and every-word inspection support safe creative iteration.
red_flags: Underlying SVGent appears pre-existing; challenge contribution is the WebMCP-bound studio layer.
standouts: Strongest end-to-end video evidence and highly distinctive agent-on-the-stage model.
advance_reason: Top candidate: deeply demonstrated, high-leverage WebMCP interaction with exceptional creative ambition.

one_line: A meeting scheduler where human and agent participants negotiate candidate times and the organizer approves the result.
what_it_does: Runs shared scheduling sessions with votes, reasons, counter-proposals, rankings, visible logs, and organizer-only final lock-in.
leverage_rationale: Structured stateful negotiation and visible human/agent logs address the reliability problems of agents operating poll UIs, especially across multiple participants and counter-proposals.
leverage_evidence: Seven WebMCP tools support reading state, joining, voting, counter-proposing, and ranking.
All actions land in a shared log tagged HUMAN or AGENT.
Only the human organizer can accept proposals or lock the final time.
execution_rationale: The workflow and safety boundary are coherent, with an alive demo and five gallery images, but visual evidence could not be inspected.
execution_evidence: Facts report an alive demo, demo link, and five gallery images.
Description specifies equal human/agent participation and an end-to-end convergence flow.
Packet claims a first-try four-tool chain from state read to winner report.
impact_rationale: Scheduling across people is common, frustrating, and well matched to negotiated constraint handling; the product has clear practical value.
impact_evidence: Targets group scheduling over multiple constraints.
Agents can act for absent participants while humans retain final approval.
creativity_rationale: Treating scheduling as a live mixed human-agent negotiation, rather than a poll with an assistant, is a fresh and appropriately ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agents are equal participants with reasons, votes, counter-proposals, and rankings.
The shared tagged negotiation log makes agent activity mutually visible.
usability_note: The familiar candidate-time UI plus explicit agent log and organizer control should be approachable; visuals were not verifiable.
red_flags: No public repository is reported; end-to-end behavior is not independently inspectable from the packet alone.
standouts: Mixed human/agent real-time negotiation with organizer-only final lock.
advance_reason: Clear high-value problem and strong shared-state WebMCP fit with a memorable negotiation model.
